analysis: The production source changes in this batch are comment-only. EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift head lines 201-203 rewrite the doc comment, and the nativeKVBytesPerToken logic at head lines 205-216 is unchanged. EngineV2KVSizing.swift head lines 8-10 change only the header comment, which now says slot assembly prices observed native per-layer types via EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken. No executable code changes appear here. The test fixture SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift (head lines 45-48) switches the gpt-oss-20b dtypes from bf16 + 23x fp32 to 24x bf16. SegmentedProductionGrantTests.swift head lines 82-84 now expect gpt-oss fullKVBytesPerToken == 24_576, the fp16 rate, instead of 49_152. This reflects a premise that the SDK now keeps bf16 K/V on every layer. These edits do not touch encryption, attestation, authorization, the cache-salt/SSD paths (T-041) or the coordinator-provider protocol (TB-002/TB-011). The only security-adjacent concern is availability/memory accounting under TB-007/T-029. If production slot pricing (EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken, not supplied) under-prices KV because the observed dtypes were wrong, admission could over-commit unified memory and cause OOM or denial of service. However, the head comment says production observes native types rather than assuming them, and the ProcessMemoryLedger live-headroom check still bounds reservations (test head lines 260-279). Integration should confirm that EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken derives per-layer dtypes from the actually allocated caches and fails closed (over-reserves) when types are unknown. The test change alone weakens regression coverage for the fp32 case but is not a production regression.
